flashcard_questions.a: A couple and their children living together as a basic social unit.
A family that reaches beyond parents and children to include other relatives.
A family formed when a divorced or widowed person remarries and brings children with them.

flashcard_questions.q: What is polygamy in the context of marriage?
flashcard_questions.a: Having more than one spouse at the same time.

flashcard_questions.q: What is bigamy under UK law?
flashcard_questions.a: The offence of marrying someone while already married to another person.

flashcard_questions.q: What does procreation mean as a purpose of family?
Which Bible verse commands people to “be fruitful and increase in number”?
What does the Church of England say about the importance of the family?
flashcard_questions.a: It is the most important grouping human beings have ever developed.

flashcard_questions.q: What does the Hadith say about the status of mothers?
flashcard_questions.a: Heaven is under the feet of the mothers.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Qur’an verse commands kindness to parents alongside worship of Allah alone?
What does 1 Timothy 5:8 say about providing for your household?
flashcard_questions.a: Anyone who fails to provide for their household has denied the faith.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do some traditional Christians disapprove of same-sex parenting?
flashcard_questions.a: They believe children should grow up with both a male and a female role model.

flashcard_questions.q: What argument do other Christians give in favour of same-sex parenting?
flashcard_questions.a: A secure and loving home matters more than the gender of the parents.

flashcard_questions.q: How many wives may a man marry under Shari’ah law?
flashcard_questions.a: Up to four, provided he treats them all equally.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do critics argue polygamy can harm children?
flashcard_questions.a: Children may see their parents less if a father keeps several households.

notes: 15 cards: 6 term→definition (nuclear, extended, blended family, polygamy, bigamy, procreation), 4 belief→source (Genesis 1:28, Qur’an 17:23, Hadith on mothers, 1 Timothy 5:8), 2 tradition→position (Church of England, Shari’ah on polygamy), 3 argument→view (same-sex parenting for and against, polygamy). Dropped 'family' and 'stability' as too generic to test.
